evidence.note: Reports score 209/780 (26.8%), notes it improved from 15.9%, and identifies 375 gcc_torture compile failures — aggregate tracking over time plus rough failure attribution used to pick next fix.

Detected regression: score dropped 294→277, suspected recent parser edits introduced regressions, ran cargo clean + rebuild to verify build integrity and re-ran suite to confirm — but only at aggregate level, never identifying which specific tests regressed.
Maintains per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) and uses the trend to decide to prioritize the closer-to-passing c-testsuite/wacc standard-C tests.

Repeatedly re-lists the same remaining bug categories (ternary, nested -> access, segfaults, GCC extensions) across many steps in prose rather than a structured ledger; does not detect its own circular re-debugging of these items.

reasoning: The agent solidly exceeds anchor 5: it tracks aggregate pass counts over the whole build, adds per-suite breakdowns, notices when a change lowers the count (294→277), and re-runs to confirm net progress. It moves toward anchor 8 by using suite-level trends to steer where to work, but falls short of it: regressions are caught only at the aggregate level (never pinpointing which tests broke), the pass/fail 'picture by feature' is recurring prose rather than a maintained ledger, and it doesn't check for regressions after each change or catch its own repeated re-debugging of the same bugs. This places the observed behavior at 6.
